title: The Living Redline
concept: A warm drafting sheet makes the P&ID story tangible: original symbols are inked over construction lines, persistent ports are projected below their equipment, a vermilion bypass creates a second route, and review annotations travel with the proposed drawing into a retained revision stack. All diagram data and route states are illustrative authored examples, not performed engineering or an approved design.
metaphor: An engineer's drafting bench, with registration marks, construction ink, tracing layers and a living redline.
choreography: Construction lines hold still while pump, valve and original route settle into ink.
A raised drawing strip projects equipment connection identities onto a lower port plane.
The selected state either retains one route or draws a red bypass around the valve and changes the review path count.
A local redline and its leader disclose the unresolved bypass size; calculation and review remain visibly pending.
Revision sheets settle into a retained stack; a proposed stamp accompanies source, change and pending approval markers.
interaction: Base route / Add bypass changes phase 2 geometry and route count, and is carried through the review and outcome phases. The branch joins upstream and downstream of Valve B; it does not bypass Pump A.
contributions: A reusable drafting visual language with construction lines, exact connection pins and ink/redline separation.
Projection choreography for retaining equipment and port identity without a dashboard or generic hub diagram.
A route choice that propagates into review annotations and the final revision drawing.
limitations: All geometry, identifiers and route counts are illustrative; no hydraulics, equipment sizing, rule validation or real engineering approval has been performed.
The stylized branch deliberately omits design details such as isolation devices and instrumentation, so it is a conceptual connection proposal rather than a construction P&ID.
Motion communicates assembly and traceability; it does not simulate fluid or calculated flow distribution.
resource_refs: Authored synthetic SVG geometry; no external or private assets.
